content.text: CORAL GABLES, FL - MARCH 07: Miami forward Malik Reneau (5) puts up a basket while defended by Louisville forward Mouhamed Camara (12) and guard J'Vonne Hadley (1) in the second half (also pictured, Louisville guard Adrian Wooley (14), guard Ryan Conwell (3)) as the Miami Hurricanes faced the Louisville Cardinals on March 7, 2026, at the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images By David Fernandez | Advance Local No. 7 seed Miami (FL) and No. 10 seed Missouri meet in what shapes up as one of the more competitive matchups of the NCAA Tournament’s First Round, with the Hurricanes entering at 25–8 and the Tigers at 20–12. Miami has been the more consistent team all season, earning ACC semifinal status behind balanced guard play and the brusing interior work of Malik Reneau. Meanwhile, Missouri brings volatility but high-end upside, highlighted by wins over top-tier opponents and a recent 32-point performance from forward Mark Mitchell. Oddsmakers have Miami as a slight favorite in a near pick’em game, with projections clustering around a tight, high-scoring contest. The game will be played in St. Louis, giving Missouri a quasi-home-court edge that could offset Miami’s stronger résumé, setting the stage for a classic “survive and advance” battle where execution late will likely decide the outcome. Expert Prediction: Miami vs. Mizzou Analysts at Dimers.com have run 10,000 simulations for this matchup, and the results point to a razor-thin edge for Miami, despite Mizzou’s standing as a trendy upset pick in NCAA Tournament brackets. The projected final score is Miami (FL) 75, Missouri 73 . The data reinforces just how evenly matched these teams are, with neither side separating significantly across key metrics like pace, efficiency, or scoring distribution. Expect a competitive, back-and-forth game that likely comes down to late-game execution, free throws, and which team controls the tempo in the final minutes. Best Bet: Missouri +1.5 With Dimers simulations showing only a two-point margin and Missouri actually holding a slight edge against the spread in probability models, grabbing Mizzou +1.5 provides strong value in what profiles as essentially a coin-flip game. The Tigers also benefit from a quasi-home environment in St. Louis, which could help stabilize their offensive rhythm and energy level.
